title: Games I’m Good At
text: “Hmm! Big sis, hold it in!”
Apparently, before her Rival could even move to stop her, the Assistant lunged at Ren. She grabbed him and shoved him to the ground.
“Whoa, what are you doing?!”
“To you! To someone like you!”
Straddling the fallen Ren, the Assistant clenched her fists and, with tears in her eyes, began pounding him.
“Ugh! Guh! S-stop it!”

Ren struggled as he was seriously punched in the face, but the Assistant’s attack didn’t stop. Right, left, right, left—the punches landed with enough force to sink into Ren’s face. It was terrifying… just like a furious dragon, the Assistant continued to pummel Ren’s face relentlessly, without the slightest hesitation. It’s not hard to imagine the scene.
“It’s you! If only you weren’t here, I—I wouldn’t have had to go through this! I wouldn’t have had to suffer like this!”
“E-enough already! Hundred Sword!”

Even Ren, for all his composure, snaps back at the Assistant’s attacks and unleashes a Skill, but the Assistant reportedly glared at the Skill Ren fired, then threw the staff he was holding to intercept only the part that looked like it was about to pierce him.
“Don’t mess with me! What kind of hero are you! Stop it! Everyone isn’t just a human shield to keep attacks from hitting you!”
“Guh! Agh! S-stop—you guys, s-stop him—”

It seems Ren finally fainted under the Assistant’s relentless, terrifying assault and stopped moving entirely. Keel, Sakura-chan, and the Rival could only watch the scene with stunned expressions. After all, even the Karma Dog Familia—who should have been appearing all around them—were so terrified by the Assistant’s rage that they stood at a distance, holding their breath.
“O-older sister! If you don’t stop this, the Sword Hero is going to die!”
Rival snapped back to her senses and, with great effort, reportedly pulled the Assistant from behind, forcing her to back away from Ren.
“Gaelion! Let go! I have to make him understand—more, much more! To a guy like that! My dad was killed by a guy like that!? I can’t take it anymore!”
“Wyndia, calm down!”
“The Sword Guy’s getting beaten to a pulp—”
“Whoa… this is bad! Sakura! Hurry up and carry the Sword Guy on your back—let’s get out of here!”
“Let me go! I have to teach him a lesson—more, much more! I have to make him regret being alive—just barely alive!”
“Calm down! You can’t do that! Dad would definitely be satisfied that you beat up the Sword Hero! Gaelion guarantees it!”
“Let me go! Let me goooooo—!”

And so, amid all the chaos, Keel and the others reportedly rushed to the island’s temporary infirmary with Ren, who had been beaten to a pulp. Apparently, because he’d struck her with such force, Ren suffered serious injuries, and it was decided she would receive advanced healing magic on the main island. Word of this reached my Father as well, and as a result, he was summoned back to a hotel on the main island that very night.
Well now, since Ren seemed to feel a sense of guilt toward her Assistant in the future, I thought they got along fine, but I never expected it to end like this.
“Fortunately, Ren didn’t suffer any serious injuries… well, thanks to the healing Magic, anyway. But he won’t come out of his hotel room.”
“You mean the Assistant?”
“No… I mean Ren.”

My Father scratched his head, mumbling in exasperation. In other words, Ren had shut himself away. Maybe the excruciating pain had left him traumatized, or perhaps he was cowering in fear of death. Either way, he must have realized just how weak he really is.
“I made him promise to hang in there… but after that, maybe she thought she couldn’t face me, because Wyndia ran off with Gaelion.”
“Well…” The Father gazed out the hotel window with a distant, twilight-like look in his eyes.
“Maybe I was wrong to ask him to stay calm when facing his parents’ killer… It’s my fault for pairing him up with Wyndia.”
“I think Ren himself has plenty of issues as well.”
“Yeah. We should be careful about that… What does he think his teammates are? I didn’t quite get the full picture from Motoyasu-kun’s explanation, but so this is what it was all about.”

I seem to recall that, according to my future Father, Ren was described as a loner who plays online games solo. However, I remember him fighting alongside his Assistant and Éclair without any problems in the first world. Rin must have experienced something I don’t know about.

“Maybe he’s one of those players who acts like a pro, forming a guild to mentor juniors? Hosting events that turn into reckless death runs just to skim off the profits, or wanting to show off how awesome he is to his juniors so they’ll praise him…”
“You sure know your stuff, Father.”
“Well, I do have some experience with online games, after all. I know a thing or two about guilds, too.”
“Was he part of the leadership team that ranked third on the server?”
“Yeah. I’m sure you know him, Motoyasu.”
“That’s right.”
“Still… Ren and Itsuki haven’t changed in that regard, have they? I thought Ren might be a little different.”
“Isn’t that a common desire among gamers?”

I don’t know that much about games since I only play the ones that Pig recommends, but I do understand them to some extent. I’ve played just about every game at the arcade. On a date, of course. By the way, the games I’m good at are rhythm games, dance games, and crane games.

Why those genres? I think I figured that if I mastered those three, I could get through a date without any trouble. There are plenty of chicks who are good at rhythm games, and dance games fall into that category too. As for crane games, if you manage to grab a stuffed animal for her, she’ll be thrilled. After that, if you can sing decently at karaoke, you’ve cleared the date.

Looking back now, those are really useless skills. Why do I have to spend my life trying to read a chick’s mood? In a way, being transported to another world was fate. Yes… it was fate that I would meet Filo-tan.
My Father nodded at my words.
“That’s true. I won’t say it didn’t happen… but… it seems both Ren and Itsuki were playing in an extreme way. I wonder if they even realized they were playing against human opponents.”
I know all too well how Father feels, and how Ren and the others feel.
“I understand that much of the difference. But I suppose they just can’t bring themselves to accept it.”

I’m fully aware that we viewed our fellow Heroes—who were also among the Four Saints—as Rival Heroes. We thought we’d become stronger by outsmarting them, and deep down, we looked down on their allies. And since we knew the world better than our own allies, we were absolutely unwilling to accept any objections.

That’s probably why we reacted so strongly to the objections raised by Keel, the Assistant, and our Rival Heroes. “You inferior lot shouldn’t defy me, a high-level player,” I thought. …That must have been the feeling I had toward Father during our first meeting on this island. “A former beginner who’s trying to monopolize a cute girl is acting all high and mighty…” That’s what I thought back then.

“People who play like Ren were, at best, just hired as mercenaries. In most online games, roles are divided by class, so there are plenty of situations where you can’t do anything on your own. That’s why I think someone like Ren is definitely the type you’d never—ever—take into a difficult top-tier dungeon. He’d just be a burden to everyone else.”
“That really stings.”
“How did it go with Itsuki?”
“It seems to have gone just as expected.”
“I’m worried about what’s ahead… I wonder if they’ll swap out members again after this.”
My father-in-law let out a deep sigh. Just then, near the hotel entrance, the assistant was quietly peeking in our direction.
“Big sis, go apologize already.”
“B-but…”
“It’ll be fine. Naofumi will probably scold you, but he won’t threaten you like Kou did.”
Noticing this, my father-in-law beckoned the assistant over. The assistant clasped her hands together apologetically and walked over to my Father with her head bowed.
“Um… it seems you realize you did something wrong.”
Even though she knew she was in the wrong, the assistant kept her eyes averted. It was the reaction of a child who’d just gotten into a fight.

“I can’t say I don’t understand how you feel. Ren was in the wrong too, and there’s no denying he put everyone’s lives in danger. But settling it with violence… isn’t that against the spirit of this event? After all, it’s supposed to be for the sake of friendship between heroes.”
“I… didn’t do anything wrong.”

“No, that’s not true. Everyone was at fault. I’m at fault too—I thought I was taking the feud between you and Ren seriously, but I actually took it lightly. Ren’s actions and responses were also wrong. And Wyndia-chan was at fault too.”
“But—”
“You came to see me like this because you think you did something wrong, right, Wyndia? Otherwise, I think you’d be coming to report to me proudly.”
My assistant is looking more dejected than I’ve ever seen her before.
“I won’t scold you, but let’s reflect on this, okay? Otherwise, if every time you run into Ren from now on it turns into a fight, you won’t be able to fulfill your mission, right?”
“That’s right! I’m sure this time, Dad will forgive the Sword Hero too. Gaelion guarantees it.”
“Gaelion…”
At that point, Father shifts his gaze, as if choosing his words carefully. That line just now definitely came from the parent of one of my Rival’s assistants.
“Anyway, please don’t do anything like this again. I’ll talk to Ren too, so make sure it doesn’t happen next time.”
“…Yeah. I’m sorry.”
“Yeah, it’s fine as long as you try to learn from your mistakes. I’m sorry, too. If I’d understood Wyndia a little better, this probably wouldn’t have happened.”
“The Shield Hero didn’t do anything wrong!”
As my father apologized, the Assistant shouted that out loud. That’s right. My father didn’t do anything wrong. I think Ren is mostly to blame this time.

“R-really?　“Well, it’s not all bad. After all, the fact that he couldn’t do a thing against Wyndia-chan means Ren will really realize just how strong she is. It’s not all bad, so try not to worry too much about it.”
“Yes…”
“See? Naofumi didn’t get mad as long as you properly reflected on it! Gaelion believed in Naofumi.”
“Gaelion-chan… try a little harder to rein Wyndia-chan in next time.”
“Naofumi asked me to! Gaelion will do her best!”
The Rival was snorting loudly as she playfully teased her Assistant.
“Still, I’m worried about what lies ahead… How are we going to convince Ren and Itsuki…”
“The future looks uncertain.”
“Absolutely.”
And with that, my Father, looking utterly exhausted, began trudging back toward his room.
